title: SC-300 Domain 4 questions (4.3, 4.4)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Microsoft.

questions.stem: In Privileged Identity Management, what is the key difference between an eligible assignment and an active assignment of a Microsoft Entra role?
choices: An eligible user receives only the read permissions of the role
An active user must request approval at every sign-in
An eligible user must activate the role before using it
An active assignment always ends after eight hours of use
questions.answer: An eligible user must activate the role before using it
questions.explanation: An eligible assignment gives no permissions until the user activates the role; an active assignment grants the permissions with no activation step. Eligibility does not grant a read-only subset of the role.

questions.stem: Fabrikam hires a contractor who needs the User Administrator role a few times a week for the next six months. Access must be just-in-time and must end automatically when the contract ends. Which assignment should you create in PIM?
choices: A time-bound eligible assignment that ends on the contract end date
A permanent active assignment with approval required to activate
A time-bound active assignment that ends on the contract end date
A permanent eligible assignment reviewed by a quarterly access review
questions.answer: A time-bound eligible assignment that ends on the contract end date
questions.explanation: An eligible assignment gives just-in-time access, and an end date removes it automatically when the contract ends. A time-bound active assignment would give standing access for the whole six months.

questions.stem: Contoso finds that 11 users hold permanent active assignments to the Global Administrator role. The users still need the role occasionally. You must remove standing access with the LEAST disruption to their work. What should you do?
choices: Remove their assignments and give each user the Global Reader role
Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks the Global Administrator role
Turn on approval to activate in the Global Administrator role settings
Convert their permanent active assignments to eligible assignments in PIM
questions.answer: Convert their permanent active assignments to eligible assignments in PIM
questions.explanation: Converting active assignments to eligible keeps the users able to get the role when needed while removing standing access. Requiring approval affects only activations, so it does nothing to users who are already permanently active.

questions.stem: A user at Tailwind Traders was made eligible for the Security Administrator role yesterday. Today the user says that the security settings pages are read-only. The assignment is listed correctly in PIM. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The user has not activated the eligible role assignment
The Security Administrator role cannot be managed in PIM
The role must be scoped to an administrative unit first
The user must wait for the next directory synchronization cycle
questions.answer: The user has not activated the eligible role assignment
questions.explanation: An eligible assignment grants no permissions until the user activates it in PIM. Security Administrator is fully supported in PIM, and cloud role assignments do not depend on directory synchronization.

questions.stem: Which license must users have when they are given eligible Microsoft Entra role assignments in Privileged Identity Management?
choices: Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium for each user account
Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Microsoft Entra ID Free with security defaults turned on
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or Microsoft 365 Business Premium
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance
questions.explanation: PIM is a Microsoft Entra ID P2 capability, also included in Microsoft Entra ID Governance. Microsoft Entra ID P1 includes Conditional Access but not PIM.

questions.stem: Northwind Traders wants a junior identity administrator to manage eligible and active Microsoft Entra role assignments in PIM. Following the principle of least privilege, which role should you assign?
choices: Security Administrator
User Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
Global Administrator
questions.answer: Privileged Role Administrator
questions.explanation: Privileged Role Administrator can manage role assignments and PIM settings for Microsoft Entra roles without the full tenant control of Global Administrator. Security Administrator and User Administrator cannot manage privileged role assignments.

questions.topic: PIM role settings and activation requirements
questions.stem: Litware wants users who activate the Exchange Administrator role to state why they need it and to reference the related change record. What should you configure in the role settings in PIM?
choices: Require an access review of the role every month
Require multifactor authentication on active assignment
Require justification and ticket information on activation
Require approval to activate and select the change manager
questions.answer: Require justification and ticket information on activation
questions.explanation: Justification and ticket information are separate activation settings that capture the reason and the change record. Approval adds a reviewer but does not by itself record a ticket reference.

questions.topic: PIM role settings and activation requirements
questions.stem: What is the maximum activation duration that you can configure for a Microsoft Entra role in Privileged Identity Management?
choices: 72 hours
24 hours
7 days
8 hours
questions.answer: 24 hours
questions.explanation: The maximum activation duration for a Microsoft Entra role can be set between 1 and 24 hours. Eight hours is the default, not the maximum.

questions.topic: PIM role settings and activation requirements
questions.stem: Adatum requires that Global Administrator activations happen only after phishing-resistant authentication, while other roles keep the default multifactor authentication requirement. What should you configure for the Global Administrator role?
choices: Require multifactor authentication on activation and ask administrators to register passkeys in the authentication methods policy
Create a Conditional Access policy for all users that requires a compliant device whenever any admin portal is opened
Require approval to activate and choose the security team as approvers who confirm each user's authentication method
Require a Conditional Access authentication context on activation and target it with a phishing-resistant authentication strength policy
questions.answer: Require a Conditional Access authentication context on activation and target it with a phishing-resistant authentication strength policy
questions.explanation: An authentication context on activation lets a Conditional Access policy demand a specific authentication strength for that one role. The plain multifactor authentication setting can be satisfied by any MFA method, so it does not guarantee phishing resistance.

questions.topic: PIM role settings and activation requirements
questions.stem: An administrator changes the maximum activation duration of the User Administrator role from 8 hours to 2 hours in PIM. Which assignments does the change affect?
choices: Only the User Administrator assignments created after the change
Every eligible assignment of User Administrator in the tenant
Only the user who was selected when the setting was changed in PIM
Every eligible assignment of every Microsoft Entra role
questions.answer: Every eligible assignment of User Administrator in the tenant
questions.explanation: PIM role settings are defined per role, so they apply to all assignments of that role. They do not apply to other roles, and they are not stored per user.

questions.topic: PIM role settings and activation requirements
questions.stem: The security operations team at Proseware must receive an email each time anyone activates the Global Administrator role. The activation process must not change. What should you do?
choices: Add the team's mailbox as a recipient of activation notifications in the role settings
Add the security team as approvers in the Global Administrator role settings in PIM
Assign the members of the team the Reports Reader role in the tenant
Create an access review of the role with the team as the reviewers
questions.answer: Add the team's mailbox as a recipient of activation notifications in the role settings
questions.explanation: The notification settings of a role let you add extra recipients for activation alerts without changing how users activate. Making the team approvers would add an approval step to every activation.

questions.topic: PIM role settings and activation requirements
questions.stem: Wide World Importers requires that nobody can hold an eligible assignment to the Billing Administrator role for longer than six months. What should you configure in the PIM role settings?
choices: Clear permanent eligible assignments and set eligibility to expire after six months
Require approval to activate and set approval to expire after six months
Clear permanent active assignments and set active assignments to expire after six months
Set the maximum activation duration of the role to six months
questions.answer: Clear permanent eligible assignments and set eligibility to expire after six months
questions.explanation: The assignment settings control how long eligible assignments can last, so blocking permanent eligibility with a six-month expiry meets the rule. The activation duration limits a single activation, which cannot exceed 24 hours.

questions.stem: An engineer at Contoso must manage PIM eligible assignments of Azure roles on one subscription. Following the principle of least privilege, which Azure role should the engineer have on the subscription?
choices: Owner
User Access Administrator
Contributor
Reader
questions.answer: User Access Administrator
questions.explanation: User Access Administrator can manage role assignments, including PIM assignments, without the full resource management rights of Owner. Contributor and Reader cannot manage access.

questions.stem: At which Azure scopes can Privileged Identity Management manage role assignments for Azure resources?
choices: Resource groups and individual resources, but not subscriptions
Administrative units, subscriptions and resource groups
Subscriptions only, inherited by all their resource groups
Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources
questions.answer: Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources
questions.explanation: PIM for Azure resources works at every Azure RBAC scope: management group, subscription, resource group and individual resource. Administrative units are a Microsoft Entra scope, not an Azure one.

questions.stem: Developers at Fabrikam need the Contributor role on the production resource group only when fixing incidents, and their team lead must agree to each request. What should you do?
choices: Make the developers eligible for Contributor on the resource group and require approval in its role settings
Assign the developers Contributor on the subscription and use a resource lock on the production resource group
Assign the developers a custom Azure role that copies Contributor and set the assignment to expire after one year
Make the developers eligible for the Application Administrator role and require approval in its role settings
questions.answer: Make the developers eligible for Contributor on the resource group and require approval in its role settings
questions.explanation: An eligible Azure role assignment at the resource group scope with approval required gives just-in-time access that the team lead approves. Application Administrator is a Microsoft Entra role and grants nothing on Azure resources.

questions.stem: A user activates an eligible Reader assignment that was made at a management group in PIM. What can the user read while the role is active?
choices: All Microsoft Entra objects in the tenant directory
Only the resource groups that were named in the activation request
All subscriptions and resources under the management group
Only the management group object and its own settings, not child scopes
questions.answer: All subscriptions and resources under the management group
questions.explanation: Azure role assignments are inherited down the scope hierarchy, so a role activated at a management group applies to every subscription and resource beneath it. Azure roles do not grant access to Microsoft Entra directory objects.

questions.stem: Tailwind Traders wants eligible Owner role holders on the finance subscription to give a justification and to be limited to four hours per activation. Other subscriptions must keep their current settings. Where should you configure this?
choices: The PIM role settings for Owner on the finance subscription
An Azure Policy assignment on the finance subscription's resources
A Conditional Access policy with a sign-in frequency control
The PIM role settings for the Global Administrator role
questions.answer: The PIM role settings for Owner on the finance subscription
questions.explanation: Role settings for Azure resources are defined per role at each resource scope, so changing Owner on the finance subscription leaves other subscriptions untouched. Azure Policy governs resource configuration, not PIM activation rules.

questions.stem: Which kinds of group assignment can be managed just-in-time by using PIM for Groups?
choices: Group membership and group ownership
Group naming policy and group classification
Dynamic membership rules and group expiration
Group ownership only, for Microsoft 365 groups
questions.answer: Group membership and group ownership
questions.explanation: PIM for Groups supports eligible and active assignments for both the member and the owner of a group. Dynamic membership rules and naming policies are not PIM features.

questions.stem: Support engineers at Litware need the Helpdesk Administrator, Groups Administrator and License Administrator roles together during their shift, and they must get all three with a single activation. What should you do?
choices: Assign the three roles to a role-assignable group and make the engineers eligible members through PIM for Groups
Make the engineers eligible for each of the three roles and ask them to activate the three roles one after another each shift
Assign the three roles to a dynamic membership group whose rule matches the department of the engineers
Add the engineers to an administrative unit and assign the three roles to the administrative unit itself
questions.answer: Assign the three roles to a role-assignable group and make the engineers eligible members through PIM for Groups
questions.explanation: Activating eligible membership of a role-assignable group grants every role assigned to that group at once. Separate eligible roles need three activations, and dynamic membership groups cannot be role-assignable.

questions.stem: You need to assign Microsoft Entra roles to a security group that was created last year without the option to allow role assignment. What should you do?
choices: Create a new group with role assignment enabled and use it instead
Convert the existing security group into a Microsoft 365 group
Onboard the existing group to PIM for Groups to enable role assignment
Turn on role assignment in the properties of the existing security group
questions.answer: Create a new group with role assignment enabled and use it instead
questions.explanation: Whether a group can be assigned Microsoft Entra roles is set only when the group is created and cannot be changed afterward. Onboarding a group to PIM for Groups does not make it role-assignable.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups can NOT be managed by using PIM for Groups?
choices: A role-assignable security group created in the cloud
A cloud-only security group with assigned membership
A Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership
A group whose membership is synchronized from on-premises Active Directory
questions.answer: A group whose membership is synchronized from on-premises Active Directory
questions.explanation: PIM for Groups works with cloud groups that have assigned membership; groups synchronized from on-premises Active Directory are managed there, so PIM cannot change their membership. Both security and Microsoft 365 groups are supported.

questions.stem: Payroll specialists at Adatum need access to a payroll SaaS application only during month-end processing, and access must be just-in-time. Users get access to the application through group assignment. What should you do?
choices: Make the specialists eligible for the Application Administrator role
Create a Conditional Access policy with a short sign-in frequency
Make the specialists eligible members of the group assigned to the application
Assign the application to each specialist as an individual user
questions.answer: Make the specialists eligible members of the group assigned to the application
questions.explanation: PIM for Groups lets the specialists activate membership of the group that is assigned to the application only when they need it. Application Administrator would let them manage the application rather than just use it.

questions.stem: You turn on approval to activate for a Microsoft Entra role in PIM but do not select any approvers. Who can approve activation requests for the role?
choices: Security Administrators and Security Operators
Nobody, because the request is approved automatically
The manager that is listed on each requestor's user profile
Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators
questions.answer: Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators
questions.explanation: When no specific approvers are chosen for a Microsoft Entra role, Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators are the default approvers. PIM does not route requests to the requestor's manager.

questions.stem: An approver for the Exchange Administrator role is also eligible for the role and submits an activation request. What happens to the request?
choices: The request is escalated to Global Administrators for verification of the approver identity
The request is denied immediately, because approvers cannot be eligible users
The request is activated immediately, because the requestor is an approver
Another approver must approve it, because approvers cannot approve their own requests
questions.answer: Another approver must approve it, because approvers cannot approve their own requests
questions.explanation: PIM does not let an approver approve their own activation request, so another approver must act on it. Being an approver does not stop a user from also holding an eligible assignment.

questions.stem: A user at Proseware submits a request to activate the SharePoint Administrator role and then finds out that the task has been cancelled. The request is still waiting for approval. What should the user do?
choices: Ask an approver to deny the activation request
Ask an administrator to remove the eligible assignment
Cancel the pending activation request in PIM
Wait for the role to activate and then ignore it
questions.answer: Cancel the pending activation request in PIM
questions.explanation: A requestor can cancel their own pending request, which leaves no unneeded activation behind. Waiting for activation would create privileged access that nobody needs.

questions.stem: A user activates the Intune Administrator role for eight hours but finishes the task after one hour. To follow the principle of least privilege, what should the user do?
choices: Deactivate the role assignment in PIM
Sign out of the Microsoft Intune admin center
Change the role's maximum activation duration
Remove their eligible assignment in PIM
questions.answer: Deactivate the role assignment in PIM
questions.explanation: Deactivating ends the active assignment early while keeping the user eligible for the future. Signing out of a portal does not remove the active role.

questions.stem: An analyst at Northwind Traders has a time-bound eligible assignment to the Security Reader role that ends in five days. The analyst still needs the role next quarter. What should the analyst do?
choices: Ask an administrator for a permanent active assignment instead
Request an extension of the eligible assignment in PIM
Submit a new activation request every day
Activate the role now for the longest activation duration allowed
questions.answer: Request an extension of the eligible assignment in PIM
questions.explanation: Users can request an extension of an eligible assignment that is about to expire, and an administrator approves it. Activating the role does not extend the eligibility end date.

questions.topic: PIM audit history, alerts and access reviews
questions.stem: An auditor at Contoso needs a list of everyone who activated the Global Administrator role during the past two weeks, with the times and justifications. Where should you get this information?
choices: The provisioning logs in the Microsoft Entra admin center
The Identity Secure Score history
The PIM audit history for Microsoft Entra roles
The service principal sign-in logs for that period
questions.answer: The PIM audit history for Microsoft Entra roles
questions.explanation: PIM audit history records activations, assignments and approvals, including justifications. Sign-in logs show authentications, not role activations.

questions.topic: PIM audit history, alerts and access reviews
questions.stem: Compliance at Fabrikam requires that records of PIM role activations be kept for two years. What should you do?
choices: Export the PIM audit history to a CSV file once each year
Increase the audit retention period in the role settings of PIM
Send the Microsoft Entra audit logs to a storage account or Log Analytics workspace
Create an access review of all privileged roles every two years
questions.answer: Send the Microsoft Entra audit logs to a storage account or Log Analytics workspace
questions.explanation: PIM activity is written to the Microsoft Entra audit logs, and a diagnostic setting can keep those logs for as long as needed. Built-in retention is only about 30 days (7 days on the Free tier), so a yearly export would lose most of the records.

questions.topic: PIM audit history, alerts and access reviews
questions.stem: PIM raises the alert 'Roles are being assigned outside of Privileged Identity Management'. What does this alert indicate?
choices: An approver approved a request without entering a reason in the portal
A privileged role was assigned directly instead of through PIM
An eligible assignment was extended beyond its end date
A user activated a privileged role from outside the corporate network
questions.answer: A privileged role was assigned directly instead of through PIM
questions.explanation: This alert detects role assignments made outside PIM, which bypass activation, approval and auditing controls. It is not related to network location.

questions.topic: PIM audit history, alerts and access reviews
questions.stem: PIM shows the alert 'Administrators aren't using their privileged roles' for several users. What is the BEST response?
choices: Convert the users' eligible assignments to permanent active ones
Increase the maximum activation duration for each of the roles
Dismiss the alert, because unused privileged roles cannot cause any risk
Review the assignments and remove the roles the users no longer need
questions.answer: Review the assignments and remove the roles the users no longer need
questions.explanation: Unused privileged assignments enlarge the attack surface, so they should be reviewed and removed. Making them permanently active would increase the risk.

questions.topic: PIM audit history, alerts and access reviews
questions.stem: Litware must confirm each quarter that every user who is eligible for the Privileged Authentication Administrator role still needs it, with the LEAST administrative effort. What should you configure?
choices: A Conditional Access policy for the role holders
A recurring access review of the role in PIM
A PIM security alert for unused privileged roles
A quarterly export of the PIM audit history
questions.answer: A recurring access review of the role in PIM
questions.explanation: A recurring access review asks reviewers each quarter to confirm or remove the role assignments and can apply the results automatically. Audit exports and alerts show activity but do not collect decisions.

questions.stem: What does Microsoft recommend for the accounts and domain used for emergency access?
choices: Two federated accounts that use the primary custom domain of the company
One cloud-only account for each Global Administrator
One account synchronized from on-premises Active Directory
At least two cloud-only accounts that use the onmicrosoft.com domain
questions.answer: At least two cloud-only accounts that use the onmicrosoft.com domain
questions.explanation: Cloud-only accounts in the onmicrosoft.com domain do not depend on federation, synchronization or on-premises systems, and having at least two avoids a single point of failure. Synchronized or federated accounts fail when those systems fail.

questions.stem: How should you assign the Global Administrator role to the emergency access accounts in a tenant that uses PIM?
choices: As a time-bound active assignment renewed monthly
As an eligible assignment with a 24-hour activation
As a permanent active assignment
As an eligible assignment that requires approval
questions.answer: As a permanent active assignment
questions.explanation: Emergency access accounts must work even when PIM, approvers or other services are unavailable, so they hold the role permanently and actively. An eligible assignment depends on the very activation process that might be broken.

questions.stem: The security team at Adatum must be alerted within minutes whenever an emergency access account signs in. What should you configure?
choices: Create a recurring access review that targets the emergency access accounts
Turn on a user risk policy that includes the emergency access accounts
Track the Identity Secure Score each day for changes caused by the accounts
Send sign-in logs to Log Analytics and create an alert rule on a query for the accounts
questions.answer: Send sign-in logs to Log Analytics and create an alert rule on a query for the accounts
questions.explanation: An Azure Monitor log alert on the sign-in logs in a Log Analytics workspace fires whenever the accounts are used. Risk policies act only on detected risk, and access reviews run on a schedule.

questions.stem: Multifactor authentication is enforced for sign-ins to the Azure portal and the Microsoft Entra admin center, including for emergency access accounts. Which authentication method should you register for each emergency access account?
choices: Microsoft Authenticator push notifications on a personal phone
A FIDO2 security key stored securely and separately from the other account's key
Voice calls to the main switchboard number of the company
SMS codes sent to the mobile phone of the IT manager on call
questions.answer: A FIDO2 security key stored securely and separately from the other account's key
questions.explanation: A phishing-resistant FIDO2 key, kept in a secure place and separate from the other account's credentials, does not depend on any one person or phone. SMS and phone methods tie the account to an individual and are weaker.

questions.stem: You are creating a Conditional Access policy that requires compliant devices for all users. How should you handle the emergency access accounts?
choices: Convert the accounts to guest users before enabling it
Exclude the emergency access accounts from the policy
Disable the accounts until the policy has been tested
Include the accounts so that their sign-ins are also protected
questions.answer: Exclude the emergency access accounts from the policy
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends excluding emergency access accounts from any Conditional Access policy that blocks or restricts sign-in, so a misconfigured policy cannot lock everyone out. Disabled accounts cannot be used in an emergency, and including the accounts risks the very lockout they exist to prevent.

questions.topic: PIM role settings and activation requirements
questions.stem: Match each requirement for activating a Microsoft Entra role to the PIM role setting that meets it.

pairs.item: Users must state why they need the role
Users must reference a change record
A team lead must agree before the role becomes active
Activated access must end after two hours
Users must satisfy a stricter Conditional Access policy

questions.explanation: Each activation requirement has its own role setting: justification, ticket information, approval, maximum duration and authentication context. Allowing permanent active assignment removes activation entirely, so it meets none of these needs.

questions.stem: A user is eligible for a Microsoft Entra role that requires MFA and approval to activate. Put the activation steps in the order they happen.
items: The user opens their eligible roles in PIM and selects Activate
The user completes the MFA challenge and enters a justification
The approvers receive a notification of the pending request
An approver reviews the justification and approves the request
The role assignment becomes active for the requested duration
The active assignment ends automatically when the duration expires
questions.explanation: The user starts the request and meets the activation requirements, the approvers are notified and one approves, and only then does the role become active. The active assignment ends on its own when the activation duration expires.

questions.topic: PIM audit history, alerts and access reviews
questions.stem: Match each need to the PIM feature that BEST meets it.

pairs.item: See your own past activations and requests
See every activation of a role across the tenant
Be warned that a role does not require MFA to activate
Have reviewers confirm each quarter who still needs a role
Find permanent assignments to convert to eligible

questions.explanation: My audit shows a user's own history, resource audit shows all activity for roles, alerts flag risky configurations, access reviews collect decisions and Discovery and insights finds standing access. Provisioning logs cover app provisioning, not PIM.

questions.stem: Contoso is setting up two emergency access accounts. Which TWO practices should the company follow?
choices: Store the credentials of each account in a separate secure location
Monitor and alert on every sign-in by the emergency access accounts
Synchronize the accounts from on-premises Active Directory
Register the IT director's personal phone as the only MFA method
Make the accounts eligible for Global Administrator in PIM
Disable the accounts and enable them only during an emergency
answers: Store the credentials of each account in a separate secure location
Monitor and alert on every sign-in by the emergency access accounts
questions.explanation: Keeping each account's credentials separate avoids a single point of failure, and alerting on every sign-in detects misuse. Synchronized, eligible, disabled or single-person-dependent accounts can all fail exactly when they are needed.

questions.stem: Which type of Microsoft Entra sign-in log records sign-ins that a client app performs on behalf of a user, such as refreshing a token, without the user entering anything?
choices: Managed identity sign-ins
Service principal sign-ins
Non-interactive user sign-ins
Interactive user sign-ins
questions.answer: Non-interactive user sign-ins
questions.explanation: Non-interactive user sign-ins are done by a client for a user, for example with a refresh token. Service principal sign-ins involve no user at all.

questions.stem: An Azure Functions app at Contoso uses a system-assigned managed identity to read secrets from Azure Key Vault. Where should you look to review the identity's authentications?
choices: Service principal sign-ins
Provisioning logs
Managed identity sign-ins
Non-interactive user sign-ins
questions.answer: Managed identity sign-ins
questions.explanation: Authentications by managed identities have their own sign-in log category. Service principal sign-ins cover apps that authenticate with their own secrets or certificates.

questions.stem: A user at Fabrikam cannot open SharePoint Online. The user's sign-in event shows error code 53003. What should you do NEXT?
choices: Review the Conditional Access details of the sign-in event
Check the provisioning logs for the SharePoint Online enterprise app
Unlock the user account that smart lockout has temporarily locked
Reset the user's password and require a change at sign-in
questions.answer: Review the Conditional Access details of the sign-in event
questions.explanation: Error 53003 means the sign-in was blocked by Conditional Access, and the event's Conditional Access details show which policy blocked it and why. A password reset does not fix a policy block.

questions.stem: Tailwind Traders wants to find sign-ins that still use legacy authentication protocols such as IMAP and POP before blocking them. Which sign-in log filter should you use?
choices: Token issuer type
Correlation ID
Resource
Client app
questions.answer: Client app
questions.explanation: The client app filter separates modern authentication clients from legacy clients such as Exchange ActiveSync, IMAP and POP. The resource filter shows what was accessed, not the protocol used.

questions.stem: A user opens a support case with Microsoft about a failed sign-in. Which information from the sign-in event BEST helps Microsoft find the exact event?
choices: The request ID and correlation ID
The IP address and the location
The user's object ID and user principal name
The application name and app ID
questions.answer: The request ID and correlation ID
questions.explanation: The request ID and correlation ID uniquely identify the sign-in flow in Microsoft's back-end logs. An IP address and location are shared by many sign-ins.

questions.stem: Which sign-in log property shows whether a sign-in needed single-factor or multifactor authentication?
choices: Conditional Access status
Client app
Authentication requirement
Cross-tenant access type
questions.answer: Authentication requirement
questions.explanation: The authentication requirement property is single-factor or multifactor for each sign-in. Conditional Access status only shows whether policies succeeded, failed or did not apply.

questions.stem: An app registration at Litware was deleted yesterday. You must find out who deleted it. Which log should you check?
choices: Provisioning logs
Audit logs
Identity Protection risk detections
Sign-in logs
questions.answer: Audit logs
questions.explanation: Directory changes such as deleting an app registration are recorded in the audit logs together with the actor. Sign-in logs record authentications, not changes.

questions.stem: User provisioning to a SaaS application uses the Microsoft Entra provisioning service. A new employee was not created in the app, and the provisioning logs show the status Skipped for that user. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The application's SCIM endpoint was offline during the cycle
The user is not assigned to the app or fails a scoping filter
The admin credentials for the app's SCIM endpoint have expired
The user's account was blocked by a Conditional Access policy
questions.answer: The user is not assigned to the app or fails a scoping filter
questions.explanation: Skipped means the service evaluated the user and intentionally took no action, usually because the user is out of scope. An offline endpoint or bad credentials produce failures, not skips.

questions.stem: Adatum uses HR-driven inbound provisioning from Workday to create user accounts. Several new hires have no account. Which log should you review FIRST?
choices: Sign-in logs
Risk detections
Audit logs
Provisioning logs
questions.answer: Provisioning logs
questions.explanation: The provisioning logs show each object the provisioning service processed and the result of each step. Audit logs record directory changes but give less detail about why provisioning did not happen.

questions.stem: In a Microsoft Entra audit log entry, which property tells you who performed the change?
choices: Correlation ID
Initiated by (actor)
Target(s)
Category
questions.answer: Initiated by (actor)
questions.explanation: Initiated by identifies the user or app that performed the activity. Targets list the objects that were changed.

questions.stem: The security team at Proseware must review every change made to Conditional Access policies last week. What should you use?
choices: Sign-in logs filtered on Conditional Access status
Audit logs filtered to the Conditional Access service
Provisioning logs filtered on the Conditional Access app
The Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook
questions.answer: Audit logs filtered to the Conditional Access service
questions.explanation: Policy creations, updates and deletions are directory changes, so they are in the audit logs. The insights workbook shows the effect of policies on sign-ins, not who changed them.

questions.stem: Northwind Traders suspects a consent phishing attack. You must find which users granted consent to applications last month. Where should you look?
choices: Sign-in logs, for the interactive user sign-in events
Audit logs, for the consent to application activity
Provisioning logs, for the enterprise applications in the tenant
Identity Secure Score, for the improvement actions
questions.answer: Audit logs, for the consent to application activity
questions.explanation: Consent grants are recorded in the audit logs as consent to application activities, with the user and the app. Sign-in logs show later use of the app but not the grant itself.

questions.stem: Contoso must keep Microsoft Entra sign-in logs for seven years at the lowest cost. The logs are rarely read. Which diagnostic setting destination should you use?
choices: Partner solution
Azure storage account
Azure Event Hubs
Log Analytics workspace
questions.answer: Azure storage account
questions.explanation: A storage account is the cheapest place to archive logs for a long time. A Log Analytics workspace supports queries but costs more for long retention.

questions.stem: Fabrikam uses a third-party SIEM and must stream Microsoft Entra audit and sign-in logs to it in near real time. Which diagnostic setting destination should you use?
choices: Azure Blob change feed
Azure storage account
Azure Event Hubs
Log Analytics workspace
questions.answer: Azure Event Hubs
questions.explanation: Event Hubs is the destination for streaming logs to external SIEM and monitoring tools. A storage account archives logs but does not stream them.

questions.stem: Tailwind Traders wants to analyze Microsoft Entra logs with KQL and use the built-in identity workbooks. Which diagnostic setting destination should you use?
choices: Azure Data Box
Azure storage account
Log Analytics workspace
Azure Event Hubs
questions.answer: Log Analytics workspace
questions.explanation: Workbooks and KQL queries run against a Log Analytics workspace. Logs in a storage account or event hub cannot be queried by the built-in workbooks.

questions.stem: You must create a diagnostic setting that exports Microsoft Entra logs. Following the principle of least privilege, which Microsoft Entra role should you have?
choices: Security Administrator
Global Administrator
Reports Reader
Security Reader
questions.answer: Security Administrator
questions.explanation: Security Administrator can configure diagnostic settings for Microsoft Entra logs without the full rights of Global Administrator. Security Reader and Reports Reader can read logs but cannot change export settings.

questions.stem: An administrator configured a diagnostic setting that sends only the AuditLogs and SignInLogs categories to a workspace. An analyst cannot find token refresh activity by a desktop app. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs category was not selected
The workspace retention is shorter than one day for those tables
The ServicePrincipalSignInLogs category was not selected
Token refresh activity is never logged by Microsoft Entra ID at all
questions.answer: The NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs category was not selected
questions.explanation: Token refreshes by a client on a user's behalf are non-interactive sign-ins, a separate category that must be selected. Service principal sign-ins cover apps signing in as themselves.

questions.stem: The security team at Litware wants to see which applications call Microsoft Graph, and with which HTTP requests, by sending the data to a workspace. Which log category should you add to the diagnostic setting?
choices: ProvisioningLogs
MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
AuditLogs
ServicePrincipalSignInLogs
questions.answer: MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
questions.explanation: Microsoft Graph activity logs record the HTTP requests that apps and users make to Microsoft Graph. Service principal sign-in logs show only the authentication, not the API calls made afterward.

questions.stem: Microsoft Entra logs are sent to a Log Analytics workspace. Which table holds interactive user sign-ins?
choices: AADProvisioningLogs
AuditLogs
SigninLogs
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
questions.answer: SigninLogs
questions.explanation: Interactive user sign-ins are stored in the SigninLogs table. Non-interactive sign-ins are in their own table, AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs.

questions.stem: You must count failed interactive sign-ins per user over the last day. Which KQL query should you run?
choices: SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) and ResultType != "0" | summarize count() by UserPrincipalName
SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) and ResultType != "0" | project count() by UserPrincipalName
SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) and ResultType == "0" | summarize count() by UserPrincipalName
AuditLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) and Result != "success" | summarize count() by UserPrincipalName
questions.answer: SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) and ResultType != "0" | summarize count() by UserPrincipalName
questions.explanation: A ResultType of "0" means success, so failures are any other value, and summarize count() by groups them per user. The project operator selects columns and cannot aggregate.

questions.stem: Which KQL operator returns only the columns you name, such as UserPrincipalName and IPAddress?
choices: extend
summarize
where
project
questions.answer: project
questions.explanation: project keeps only the listed columns. extend adds calculated columns while keeping all the existing ones.

questions.stem: You need to find interactive sign-ins that no Conditional Access policy applied to. Which filter should you add to a query on SigninLogs?
choices: where ConditionalAccessStatus == "failure"
where ConditionalAccessStatus == "success"
where AuthenticationRequirement == "notApplied"
where ConditionalAccessStatus == "notApplied"
questions.answer: where ConditionalAccessStatus == "notApplied"
questions.explanation: ConditionalAccessStatus is "notApplied" when no policy applied to the sign-in. "failure" means a policy applied and its controls were not met.

questions.stem: You must list every Microsoft Entra role assignment made in the past week, as recorded in the workspace. Which query should you start with?
choices: SigninLogs | where OperationName == "Add member to role"
AADProvisioningLogs | where Action == "Add member to role"
AuditLogs | where OperationName == "Add member to group"
AuditLogs | where OperationName == "Add member to role"
questions.answer: AuditLogs | where OperationName == "Add member to role"
questions.explanation: Role assignments are directory changes logged in AuditLogs with the operation "Add member to role". Group membership changes use a different operation name.

questions.stem: An analyst wants a chart of interactive sign-ins per hour over the last day. Which KQL should follow SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)?
choices: | summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) | render timechart
| extend count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) | render piechart
| project count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) | render timechart
| summarize count() by TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName | render columnchart
questions.answer: | summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) | render timechart
questions.explanation: bin() groups events into hourly buckets, summarize counts them, and render timechart draws the trend. Without bin(), each distinct timestamp becomes its own group.

questions.stem: Adatum has several Conditional Access policies in report-only mode. You must see how many sign-ins each policy would have blocked if it were enabled. What should you use?
choices: The Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook
The audit logs filtered to the Conditional Access service
The authentication methods activity report
The Sign-ins using legacy authentication workbook for each policy
questions.answer: The Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook
questions.explanation: The insights and reporting workbook shows the effect of each policy, including report-only results, across sign-ins. Audit logs show changes to policies, not their effect.

questions.stem: Before blocking legacy authentication, Fabrikam wants a view of which users and apps still use it over time. Which workbook BEST fits this need?
choices: Sensitive operations report
Authentication prompts analysis
Sign-ins using legacy authentication
App consent audit
questions.answer: Sign-ins using legacy authentication
questions.explanation: The legacy authentication workbook summarizes sign-ins by legacy protocol, user and app. Authentication prompts analysis focuses on how often users are asked to authenticate.

questions.stem: What is required before most Microsoft Entra workbooks can show data?
choices: Microsoft Entra logs must be streamed to Azure Event Hubs
Identity Protection policies must be in enforcement mode
Each user who appears in the logs must have a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license
Microsoft Entra logs must be sent to a Log Analytics workspace
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra logs must be sent to a Log Analytics workspace
questions.explanation: Workbooks query data in a Log Analytics workspace, so a diagnostic setting must send the logs there first. Event Hubs streams logs out and cannot be queried by workbooks.

questions.stem: Litware wants to know how many users have registered for multifactor authentication and self-service password reset, and which methods they use. Which report should you use?
choices: Authentication methods activity
Usage and insights for applications
Provisioning logs summary
Identity Secure Score improvement history
questions.answer: Authentication methods activity
questions.explanation: The authentication methods activity report shows registration and usage of authentication methods, including MFA and SSPR. Identity Secure Score shows overall posture, not per-method registration.

questions.stem: An internal auditor at Proseware must read sign-in and audit logs in the Microsoft Entra admin center and must not be able to read other directory settings. Following the principle of least privilege, which role should you assign?
choices: Global Reader
Reports Reader
Security Administrator
User Administrator
questions.answer: Reports Reader
questions.explanation: Reports Reader can read sign-in and audit reports and little else. Global Reader can read almost every setting in the tenant, which is more than needed.

questions.stem: Users at Contoso complain that they are asked to sign in and complete MFA too often. Which workbook BEST helps you find where the extra prompts come from?
choices: Sign-ins using legacy authentication
Cross-tenant access activity
Authentication prompts analysis
Sensitive operations report
questions.answer: Authentication prompts analysis
questions.explanation: The authentication prompts analysis workbook breaks down prompts by user, app and method, which helps tune sign-in frequency settings. The sensitive operations report looks for risky directory changes.

questions.stem: What does Identity Secure Score measure?
choices: How closely the tenant's identity settings follow Microsoft's recommended practices
How many risky sign-ins Identity Protection detected in the tenant this month
How much of the tenant's licensed capacity for Microsoft Entra ID P2 is in use
How many reviewers completed their assigned access reviews before the due date this quarter
questions.answer: How closely the tenant's identity settings follow Microsoft's recommended practices
questions.explanation: Identity Secure Score is a percentage that shows how well the tenant's identity configuration matches Microsoft's recommended improvement actions. It is not a count of risk detections.

questions.stem: Tailwind Traders protects its administrators with a third-party MFA provider, so an Identity Secure Score improvement action is already addressed. How should you record this?
choices: Leave the improvement action's status as To address and add a note
Set the improvement action's status to Risk accepted
Set the improvement action's status to Resolved through third party
Set the improvement action's status to Planned
questions.answer: Set the improvement action's status to Resolved through third party
questions.explanation: Resolved through third party records that another product meets the recommendation. Risk accepted means the organization chose not to address the risk, which is not the case here.

questions.stem: Which change would BEST improve Identity Secure Score while also protecting privileged accounts?
choices: Let users create Microsoft 365 groups without approval
Require multifactor authentication for administrative roles
Allow all users to register applications in the tenant
Turn off security defaults without any replacement policies
questions.answer: Require multifactor authentication for administrative roles
questions.explanation: Requiring MFA for administrative roles is a key improvement action that raises the score and protects the most powerful accounts. Turning off security defaults with nothing in their place lowers protection.

questions.stem: An administrator enables a recommended Conditional Access policy, but Identity Secure Score has not changed an hour later. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The score counts only improvement actions completed in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
The policy must stay in report-only mode before the score recognizes the change
The score changes only after an access review confirms the new policy
The score is recalculated periodically, so the change shows after the next refresh
questions.answer: The score is recalculated periodically, so the change shows after the next refresh
questions.explanation: Identity Secure Score is not updated in real time; the tenant's configuration is evaluated about every 24 hours and the new score appears after that calculation. Report-only mode does not earn points because it enforces nothing.

questions.stem: Identity Secure Score recommends 'Do not expire passwords'. Why does Microsoft recommend this?
choices: Password expiration is not supported for cloud-only accounts in Microsoft Entra ID
Passwords that never expire are no longer checked by Microsoft Entra Password Protection
Expiring passwords prevents multifactor authentication from working correctly
Forced periodic changes lead users to choose weaker, more predictable passwords
questions.answer: Forced periodic changes lead users to choose weaker, more predictable passwords
questions.explanation: Microsoft guidance is that forced expiration pushes users toward predictable patterns, so it is better to use MFA and banned password lists. Expiration does not break MFA.

questions.stem: Which TWO Microsoft Entra sign-in log categories record sign-ins that do NOT involve a user?
choices: Service principal sign-ins
Managed identity sign-ins
Interactive user sign-ins
Non-interactive user sign-ins
AD FS sign-ins
questions.explanation: Service principal and managed identity sign-ins are workload identities authenticating as themselves. Non-interactive user sign-ins happen without user input but are still done on behalf of a user.

questions.stem: Match each logging need to the diagnostic setting destination that BEST meets it.

pairs.item: Run KQL queries and Azure Monitor log alerts
Archive logs for years at the lowest cost
Stream logs in near real time to a third-party SIEM
Send logs to an integrated Azure Native ISV service

questions.explanation: Log Analytics supports queries and alerts, storage accounts are the cheapest archive, Event Hubs streams to external tools and partner solutions integrate with Azure Native ISV services. A Recovery Services vault holds backups and is not a log destination.

questions.stem: Contoso does not yet send any Microsoft Entra logs to Azure Monitor. Put the steps in order to query interactive sign-ins with KQL.
items: Create a Log Analytics workspace in an Azure subscription
Create a Microsoft Entra diagnostic setting that sends SignInLogs to the workspace
Wait for new sign-in events to arrive in the workspace
Run a KQL query against the SigninLogs table in the workspace
Save the query or pin its results to a workbook
questions.explanation: A workspace must exist before a diagnostic setting can target it, and only events that occur after the setting is created arrive. Then the SigninLogs table can be queried and the query saved or reused in a workbook.

questions.stem: Match each Identity Secure Score improvement action to the threat it BEST reduces.

pairs.match: Takeover of admin accounts with stolen passwords
Password spray against protocols that cannot do MFA
Use of credentials that were leaked online

pairs.item: Do not allow user consent to unverified apps
pairs.match: Illicit consent grant by a phishing app

questions.explanation: MFA protects admin accounts from stolen passwords, blocking legacy protocols stops spray attacks that bypass MFA, user risk policies respond to leaked credentials and consent restrictions stop illicit consent grants. None of these directly addresses malware on devices.
